title: Physics Mock Test No. 2
subtitle: 45 tasks • 55 scored items • 3 hours • with formula sheet and calculator

questions.text: Using the graph, determine the distance travelled by the body in the time interval (2–5) s. (m)
The initial speed of a body is 20 m/s. It is known that its speed at the end of the path reached 60 m/s. Determine its speed at the midpoint of the path (m/s). √5 = 2.2
Forces F₁ = 12 N and F₂ = 5 N act on a body of mass 6.5 kg in the horizontal direction at an angle of 90° to each other. Determine the acceleration (m/s²) with which the system will move.
A body thrown vertically upward passes the height of 40 m for the second time at the moment t = 4 s. What was the initial speed of the body (m/s)?

The three bodies shown in the figure are connected by weightless strings. Their masses are m₁ = 3 kg, m₂ = 6 kg and m₃ = 1 kg, respectively. A horizontal force F = 120 N is applied to this system. Determine the tensions T₁ and T₂ (N) in the strings. The coefficient of friction is the same for all bodies and equals 0.5.
Based on the data given in the figure, determine the acceleration (m/s²) acquired by the body.
A body sinks in kerosene with an acceleration of 4 m/s². With what acceleration will it sink in water? ρ_water = 1 g/cm³, ρ_kerosene = 0.8 g/cm³

As shown in the figure, loads of masses m₁ = 4 kg and m₂ = 6 kg are attached to the ends of a spring of stiffness 2 kN/m. The coefficient of friction for each load is 0.1. By how many centimetres will the spring stretch?
By what percentage will the period of oscillation of a simple pendulum increase when it is placed in the cabin of a high-speed lift descending with an acceleration of 0.36g?
When an ideal gas passes from the first state to the second, its temperature changes by 330 °C. If V₁ = 3.2 m³ and V₂ = 6.4 m³, what was the initial temperature of the gas (K)?
The density of an ideal gas is 1.2 kg/m³ and its pressure is 16 kPa. What is the root-mean-square speed of the gas molecules (m/s)?
The base area of a load placed on a plane is 10 cm². What pressure will the load exert on the plane if the system is moved upward with a speed of 2 m/s? The mass of the load is 4 kg.
How much heat (kJ) is released from 5 litres of water at 0 °C placed in a freezer until it freezes completely? λ = 334 kJ/kg.
To what height (cm) will water rise in a soil capillary of diameter 75 μm? Water wets the soil completely. The surface tension coefficient of water is 73 mN/m.
If the resistance of the resistor is R = 6 Ω and the current through it is I = 2 A, determine the potential difference φB − φA (V) between points B and A.

An electric circuit is made of capacitors with capacitances C₁ = 6 nF, C₂ = 2 nF and C₃ = 4 nF. Capacitors C₁ and C₂ are connected in parallel, and C₃ is connected in series with them; they are charged from a DC voltage source. If the charge on the first capacitor is 12 nC, find the charge on the third capacitor (nC).

After the external circuit is connected, the potential difference across the battery terminals is 18 V. The resistance of the external circuit is R = 6 Ω. If the emf of the battery is 30 V, find the internal resistance of the battery.

In a circuit of three identical conductors connected in parallel to the mains, a certain amount of heat is released in time t₁ = 40 s. In what time t₂ will the same amount of heat be released if these conductors are connected in series?

An electric circuit consists of resistances of 40 Ω and 10 Ω connected in parallel and a battery with emf 10 V. The current in the main circuit is I = 1 A. Determine the short-circuit current of the battery.
Find the kinetic energy of a 2 μC charge that has passed through a potential difference of 500 V starting from rest.
When a battery of 20 capacitors connected in parallel was charged, 10 J of heat was released. If the capacitance of each capacitor is 4 μF, determine the voltage across the capacitors.
A capacitor of capacitance 1 μF is connected to an AC circuit of frequency 50 Hz. Determine the capacitive reactance of the capacitor.
A force F = 0.15 N acts on a straight conductor of length l = 0.5 m placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of induction B = 2 · 10⁻² T. Find the current in the conductor.
A resistance of 40 Ω is connected in an AC circuit, and the rms value of the current is 5 A. Determine the maximum value of the voltage in the circuit.
When the length of the string of a simple pendulum is decreased by 5 cm, its frequency increases by a factor of 1.5. Find the initial length of the pendulum string.

The primary winding of a step-down transformer with a transformation ratio of 8 is connected to a 220 V mains supply. The resistance of the secondary winding is 2 Ω and the current in it is 3 A. Determine the voltage across the terminals of the secondary winding.

A lens with a focal length of 12 cm forms a real image of an object reduced 3 times. When this lens is replaced with another one, an image magnified 3 times is obtained. Determine the focal length of this lens.
The distance from an object to a converging lens is n = 5 times the focal length of the lens. How many times smaller is the image than the object?
The energy of photons incident on a metal surface is 7.8 · 10⁻¹⁹ J, and the work function of this metal is 3 · 10⁻¹⁹ J. Determine the stopping voltage for the electrons.

If the work function of electrons from a metal surface is 6 · 10⁻¹⁹ J and the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected photoelectrons is 6 · 10⁻²⁰ J, determine the wavelength (nm) of the light incident on the metal surface. Planck's constant is 6.6 · 10⁻³⁴ J·s.
What is the wavelength (nm) of light if the momentum of a photon of this light is 1.1 · 10⁻²⁷ kg·m/s? Planck's constant is 6.6 · 10⁻³⁴ J·s.

Determine by how much (kJ) the internal energy of the gas changes in the transition 2 → 3 shown in the graph if 40 kJ of heat is supplied to the gas.

questions.text: A body is released from rest at a height of 320 m.

parts.text: Determine the time of fall.
Determine the speed of the body 5 s after it was released.

questions.text: A spring of stiffness 500 N/m is attached to the ceiling of a lift, and a body of mass 2 kg is hung from it.

parts.text: By how much does the spring stretch if the system moves upward with an acceleration of 5 m/s²?
By how much is the spring deformed if the system moves downward with a speed of 5 m/s?

questions.text: Two bodies lying on a horizontal surface are connected as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between the bodies and the surface is the same and equals 0.4.

parts.text: Determine the acceleration of the system.
Determine the tension in the string connecting the bodies.

questions.text: In an isobaric process, 10 kJ of heat is supplied to a monatomic ideal gas.

parts.text: Determine the change in internal energy.
Determine the work done on the gas by external forces.

questions.text: Two bodies of mass 5 kg each move in the same direction with speeds 3 m/s and 5 m/s. The bodies collide inelastically and move together.

parts.text: Determine the speed of the system after the collision.
Determine the kinetic energy of the system of bodies after the collision.

questions.text: The resistor of resistance 11 Ω shown in the diagram is connected to a source with emf 26 V. It is known that a current of 2 A flows through the resistor:

parts.text: Determine the internal resistance of the source.
Determine the short-circuit current.

questions.text: A circuit is made of an active resistance of 5 Ω, an inductive reactance of 20 Ω and a capacitive reactance of 8 Ω connected in series.

parts.text: Find the total impedance of the circuit.
Determine what the total impedance would be if the active resistance were 0.

questions.text: A point light source is located at a distance d = 4 cm from the principal optical axis of a converging lens with focal length F = 6 cm. On the other side of the lens, a real image of the source is formed at a distance f = 12 cm from the lens.

parts.text: Determine the magnification of the lens (|m|).
Determine the distance between the light source and the lens.

questions.text: The focal length of a converging lens is F = 10 cm and the object is at a distance l = 5 cm from the focus. The linear size of the object is h = 2 cm.

parts.text: Determine the height H of the image when it is real.
Determine the height H of the image if it is virtual.

questions.text: The light energy flux density at a surface is 9 kW/m².

parts.text: Determine the pressure of light if the surface reflects the light completely.
Determine the pressure of light if the surface absorbs the light completely.
